sections.html:
LaPorte County is in the northwest corner of Indiana, on the Lake Michigan shoreline, with the city of La Porte as the county seat and Michigan City as its largest community. It covers 613.26 square miles, of which 598.30 is land, and it reaches Berrien County, Michigan to the north, St. Joseph County to the east, Starke County to the south, and Jasper and Porter counties to the west and southwest.

Part of Indiana Dunes National Park lies inside the county. Its lowest point is 581 feet on the lakeshore and its highest is 957 feet in southwestern Galena Township. Rivers and creeks include Trail Creek, the Kankakee River and the Little Calumet River.

The 11 municipalities are Kingsbury, Kingsford Heights, La Porte, LaCrosse, Long Beach, Michiana Shores, Michigan City, Pottawattamie Park, Trail Creek, Wanatah and Westville. Michigan, Center and Coolspring were the biggest townships by population in 2010.

sections.h2: What is the history behind LaPorte County?
sections.html:
The name is French for "the door," a reference to a natural opening through the dense forest. Before settlement the land belonged to the Potawatomi, who were forcibly removed to Kansas in 1838 in the Trail of Death.

The county reached its present shape after land was annexed from Starke County in 1842 and from St. Joseph County in 1850. Its population was 8,184 in 1840 and reached 112,417 in 2020, with a slight dip in the 1990s. Spelling is even disputed: state law uses LaPorte County, while the city is written La Porte.

Population has barely moved since 2010, when the census counted 111,467 people.

sections.h2: What are the main job centers in LaPorte County?
sections.html:
Michigan City is the biggest, with 32,075 residents in 2020 on Lake Michigan about 45 miles east of Chicago. Wikipedia names the Blue Chip Casino, which added a 22-story hotel in 2009, Lighthouse Place Premium Outlets, which opened in 1987, and Franciscan Health Michigan City as the main hospital. The Michigan City Generating Station, a coal plant, sits on the lakeshore.

La Porte, the county seat, had 22,471 residents in 2020. Its history is tied to Advance-Rumely, which made the Oil-Pull tractor engine and was the city's largest employer by 1869. The current county courthouse, built from Lake Superior red sandstone, dates to 1892 to 1894.

  • Michigan City: casino, outlet shopping, hospital and lakefront tourism
  • La Porte: county government, a school corporation of about 6,500 students and lakes for recreation
  • Westville: Purdue University Northwest has a campus there

sections.h2: What are LaPorte County's schools, lakes and roads like?
sections.html:
Michigan City Area Schools has one high school, two middle schools and eight elementary schools. The La Porte Community School Corporation serves about 6,500 students and covers most of its city. The La Porte High School baseball program has won eight state titles, more than any other Indiana school.

La Porte has Clear Lake, part of 170-acre Fox Memorial Park, and Pine Lake, which has a public beach.

The Indiana Toll Road carries I-80 and I-90 across the county, and US 6, US 12 and US 20 add east-west routes. The South Shore Line stops at 11th Street-Carroll Avenue in Michigan City and at Hudson Lake. Michigan City Transit has been free to ride since December 2025, and Amtrak no longer stops in the city.

sections.h2: How does lake-effect weather affect houses in LaPorte County?
sections.html:
Winters are long and snowy. La Porte averages about 65 inches of snow a year, mostly from December through February, and about 42.5 inches of precipitation. Average January lows are near 12 degrees, the record low is minus 28 from January 1977, and the record high is 104 from June 1988.

Snow load, ice dams and frozen pipes are the practical concerns for owners of older houses. Michigan City's summers are warm and humid, with frequent thunderstorms. If a roof or furnace is near the end of its life, a cash buyer takes that on as part of the purchase.

sections.h2: Which LaPorte County offices handle property tax?
sections.html:
The county complex is at 809 State St., La Porte, and it is open Monday through Friday from 8:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. Most departments use the county's main number, 219-326-6808, with an extension.

The county's tax page says to start an assessment question with the township assessor and to review the property record card first. The County Assessor oversees the township assessors, and Michigan Township has its own line at (219) 874-5611.

sections.h2: When did LaPorte County mail its 2026 assessment notices?
sections.html:
The state lists April 29, 2026 for the county's Form 11 mailing and April 22, 2026 for Michigan Township. Both carry a June 15, 2026 appeal deadline.

Under the state's rules, a notice mailed before May 1 sets a June 15 deadline in the assessment year. A notice mailed later, or no notice, pushes the deadline to June 15 of the year the treasurer mails the bill. Check whether your 2026 deadline has already passed before you plan an appeal.

If you disagree with the township assessor, the PTABOA must hold a hearing within 180 days of your petition, and notice goes out at least 30 days ahead. A missed hearing without an approved continuance can cost $50. Not-for-profit exemptions must be filed with the County Assessor by April 1.

sections.h2: How did the 2025 state law change homestead deductions in LaPorte County?
sections.html:
The standard homestead deduction is $48,000 for taxes payable in 2026, steps down to $40,000, $30,000, $20,000 and $10,000 in the following years, and ends with the 2030 assessment date. The supplemental deduction grows from 40% in 2026 to 62% in 2030 and 66.7% from 2031.

A homestead credit of the lesser of 10% of the bill or $300 started with 2026 taxes, and the over-65 credit is up to $150 for owners under the income limits. Applications for the over-65 credit are due by January 15 of the year the taxes are payable.

sections.h2: How does the LaPorte County tax sale work?
sections.html:
A parcel can be offered at the LaPorte County tax sale when the prior year's spring installment is still unpaid. The sale is typically held in October, notices go out beginning in late July, and the delinquent amount is typically due by mid-August.

  • A $220.00 administration fee is added once a property is scheduled for sale
  • Owner names and property details are published in the local newspaper and on the SRI Tax Sale Services website
  • Bidders register with SRI before the sale
  • Redemption and procedure questions go to the Auditor at 219-326-6808 ext. 2004
  • The Treasurer sends notice of surplus when a payment exceeds $5.00

The county's real estate tax sale page has the current advertisement and parcel list.

sections.h2: What should a LaPorte County seller know about paying tax before closing?
sections.html:
Taxes can be paid at the Treasurer's offices, at local banks that accept them, or by mail with a federal postmark no later than the deadline. Banks may set earlier cutoffs. The county suggests that an owner who cannot pay should contact the Indiana Department of Revenue about a payment plan.

The state lists May 11 and November 10 as 2026 due dates. An owner who sells with a balance outstanding usually has the closing agent pay it from the proceeds. Anyone with an unpaid spring installment should look at the tax sale timeline above, because a parcel can become eligible after the prior spring installment goes unpaid.

faqs.q: When is the LaPorte County property tax appeal deadline?
faqs.a: For 2026, the state lists June 15, 2026 for the county and Michigan Township. Later notices move the deadline to June 15 of the year the bill is mailed.

faqs.q: Where is the LaPorte County Treasurer?
faqs.a: The Treasurer has an office at 555 Michigan Avenue, Suite 102 in La Porte, plus one at 300 Washington Street, #361 in Michigan City. The county line is 219-326-6808.

faqs.q: When is the LaPorte County tax sale?
faqs.a: The county typically holds the sale in October. Notices go out beginning in late July.

faqs.q: How much is the LaPorte County tax sale fee?
faqs.a: A $220.00 tax sale administration fee is added once a property is scheduled for sale.

faqs.q: Can I sell a LaPorte County house that has unpaid taxes?
faqs.a: Yes. The tax balance can usually be paid from the sale proceeds at closing.
